item.text:
Using the local structured facts as priors, I kept this to a small cross-chapter set and did not re-pull the structured datasets already represented there.

**Core Findings**
- In 2022, Abdel Fattah el-Sisi was Egypt’s president and the formal head of state and executive power.
- The constitutional text gave the presidency significant agenda-setting and appointment power, but those formal checks did not translate into strong practical constraints in the rights/reporting record.
- The biggest inherited conditions in 2022 were the Ukraine-war shock to wheat and FX, long-running macro fragility, demographic pressure, and a weak civil-liberties environment.
- The most useful narrative events for chapter work are: the wheat shock and pound devaluation in spring 2022, El-Dabaa nuclear construction in July, the economic conference in October, COP27 in November, the protest-arrest wave around COP27, and the IMF deal in December.

**Retained Sources**
1. [President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi](https://www.presidency.eg/en/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%A9/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D8%A6%D9%8A%D8%B3/) - Presidency of the Arab Republic of Egypt, n.d. Precise fact: official biography identifies El-Sisi as Egypt’s eighth president. Period fit: office/identity anchor for 2022. Ruler attribution: direct official self-presentation. Limitations: self-authored, not independent. Contrary points: none on the page, so use only for identity and tenure.

2. [President of the Republic](https://www.parliament.gov.eg/Constitution.aspx) - Parliament of Egypt, current online constitutional text. Precise fact: articles 139, 140, 147, and 150 define the president as head of state and executive power, with six-year terms, limited consecutive terms, government-reshuffle authority, and joint state-policy setting with the cabinet. Period fit: formal authority and constraint frame in force in 2022. Ruler attribution: office-level legal authority, not personal behavior. Limitations: law-on-the-books only. Contrary points: does not show how much power was actually usable in practice.

3. [Construction permit issued for first Egyptian unit](https://nppa.gov.eg/News/Details?id=570) - Nuclear Power Plants Authority, July 1, 2022. Precise fact: ENRRA granted construction permission for El Dabaa unit 1, enabling main-stage construction. Period fit: 1B capability context in mid-2022. Ruler attribution: state nuclear decision under the Sisi administration. Limitations: official and optimistic. Contrary points: says nothing about operational readiness or broader governance quality.

4. [Ukraine crisis throws Egypt's wheat purchases into doubt](https://uk.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/ukraine-crisis-throws-egypts-wheat-purchases-into-doubt-2597713) - Reuters, March 3, 2022. Precise fact: Russia’s invasion disrupted Egyptian wheat cargoes and pushed prices up; Egypt is a major wheat importer. Period fit: inherited food-security shock at the start of 2022. Ruler attribution: external shock hitting the Sisi government. Limitations: immediate market disruption, not full policy diagnosis. Contrary points: does not by itself establish domestic mismanagement.

5. [Egypt devalues currency 14% after Ukraine war prompts dollar flight](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/egyptian-pound-drops-11-after-ukraine-war-prompts-dollar-flight-2788414) - Reuters, March 21, 2022. Precise fact: Egypt devalued the pound after war-related capital flight and FX pressure. Period fit: macro stress and policy constraint in 2022. Ruler attribution: macro policy under Sisi’s administration. Limitations: one-day news snapshot, not a full macro model. Contrary points: can also be read as an adjustment to inherited imbalances, not just policy failure.

6. [Construction starts on Egypt's first, Russian-built nuclear plant](https://www.brecorder.com/news/40187405/construction-starts-on-egypts-first-russian-built-nuclear-plant) - Reuters, July 22, 2022. Precise fact: first concrete was poured and construction began at El Dabaa after regulatory approval. Period fit: 1B infrastructure/capability context in 2022. Ruler attribution: flagship state project under El-Sisi. Limitations: project reporting does not establish broader performance. Contrary points: a major project can coexist with weak public-service outcomes.

7. [IMF Executive Board Approves 46-month US$3 billion Extended Arrangement for Egypt](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2022/12/16/pr22441-egypt-imf-executive-board-approves-46-month-usd3b-extended-arrangement) - IMF, December 16, 2022. Precise fact: IMF approved the EFF and tied it to a flexible exchange rate, fiscal consolidation, and structural reforms. Period fit: end-of-year inherited-conditions and policy-constraint anchor. Ruler attribution: external lender assessment of Egypt’s policy package. Limitations: describes agreed terms, not implementation. Contrary points: conditionality reflects lender priorities, not local legitimacy.

8. [كلمة الرئيس السيسي خلال فعاليات المؤتمر الاقتصادي - مصر 2022](https://sis.gov.eg/ar/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%A9/%D9%83%D9%84%D9%85%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D8%A6%D9%8A%D8%B3-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%B3%D9%8A-%D8%AE%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%81%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%A4%D8%AA%D9%85%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%82%D8%AA%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%AF%D9%8A-%D9%85%D8%B5%D8%B1-2022/) - State Information Service, October 23, 2022. Precise fact: Sisi frames reform as necessary, says 2011 created a severe state crisis, and emphasizes population growth and state capacity as core constraints. Period fit: ruler self-attribution for 5B/6B/7B/8B narrative context. Ruler attribution: direct speech by Sisi. Limitations: state-aligned and justificatory. Contrary points: omits costs borne by households and the repression context around dissent.

9. [نص كلمة الرئيس السيسي الختامية في قمة مبادرة تنسيق عمل المناخ في الشرق الأوسط وشرق المتوسط](https://gate.ahram.org.eg/News/3807937.aspx) - Ahram Gate, November 8, 2022. Precise fact: reports Sisi’s COP27-related closing remarks and Egypt’s summit-hosting role. Period fit: major 2022 event and favorable local-language framing. Ruler attribution: direct coverage of the president’s speech through state-aligned media. Limitations: celebratory tone, little rights or dissent context. Contrary points: not a neutral measure of COP27’s domestic political effects.

10. [«المفوضية المصرية للحقوق والحريات»: 39 حالة اختفاء قسري ضمن موجة اعتقالات «11 نوفمبر»](https://www.madamasr.com/2022/11/19/news/u/%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D9%81%D9%88%D8%B6%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%B5%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%84%D9%84%D8%AD%D9%82%D9%88%D9%82-%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AD%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%AA-39-%D8%AD/) - Mada Masr, November 19, 2022. Precise fact: local independent reporting says a rights group documented disappearances and large-scale arrests tied to the November protest wave. Period fit: 3B/4B repression and coercive-control context in late 2022. Ruler attribution: independent reporting on practices under the Sisi state. Limitations: relies on rights-group counting and opaque prosecution records. Contrary points: official authorities may dispute numbers or the legal framing.

11. [Egypt: Arrests over calls for protests during COP27 expose reality of human rights crisis](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2022/11/egypt-arrests-over-calls-for-protests-during-cop27-expose-reality-of-human-rights-crisis/) - Amnesty International, November 6, 2022. Precise fact: says hundreds were arrested before/during COP27, with at least 151 under investigation. Period fit: 3B and 4B repression context during the summit. Ruler attribution: actions by Egyptian authorities under Sisi. Limitations: advocacy framing and estimates. Contrary points: the government would likely characterize the arrests as lawful security measures.

**Compact Event Map**
- March 3, 2022: Ukraine-war disruption hits wheat imports, a core inherited vulnerability.
- March 21, 2022: The pound is devalued, signaling FX stress and limited policy room.
- April 21 and October 23, 2022: Sisi publicly frames the economic crisis as structural and long-running, not temporary.
- July 1 and July 22, 2022: El-Dabaa gets construction approval and then enters active construction, useful for 1B and state-capacity context.
- November 6 to November 19, 2022: COP27 coincides with a protest-arrest wave, making it the clearest rights-and-control event cluster of the year.
- December 16, 2022: IMF approves the rescue package and formalizes the flexible-exchange-rate / reform constraint set.

**Chapter Source Plan**
| Chapter | Best source families | Use them for |
|---|---|---|
| 1B | NPPA, Reuters nuclear | El-Dabaa capability context and state strategic projects |
| 2B | Reuters wheat/devaluation, IMF | External shocks, war spillovers, and macro strain |
| 3B | Mada Masr, Amnesty | Detentions, protest suppression, and coercive-control patterns |
| 4B | Constitution, SIS, Ahram, rights reports | Formal powers vs practical civil-liberties constraints |
| 5B | Reuters, IMF, SIS | Growth/macro stress and the administration’s reform narrative |
| 6B | SIS, IMF, Reuters | Welfare context, crisis-management claims, and inherited pressure |
| 7B | Constitution, IMF, rights reporting | Accountability, anti-corruption, and rule-of-law environment |
| 8B | Constitution, SIS, IMF, Ahram | Administrative capacity, state coordination, and official performance claims |

This is research only. No scoring was done.
